propositions: Physical deletion of committed enrichment queue events enables git rename-detection conflicts on cross-clone merges but reclaims zero repository space since blobs persist in git history.
The enrichment queue reduce performs O(history) file opens and json-parses every matching event file, causing the drain gate to breach its 20 ms budget (measured 404-544 ms) on the live tracker.

A newest-first suffix-lazy reader bounding queue reduce to 3+k file opens per ticket (bounded by event type and parse failures) is merge-safe because it removes, renames, and writes nothing—only changes read order.

The design preserves invariant I1 (no physical delete or rename of committed UUID events) by making no filesystem changes whatsoever; the two-clone regression test confirms reconvergence is unaffected.

Per-ticket accumulation of the four event types (1,885 ENQUEUE, 1,545 CLAIM, 1,547 DONE, 1,548 DIGEST across 554 tickets, median 2-3 per ticket) totals only 5.3 MiB of 251 MiB checkout, so checkout size is not the problem—read cost asymmetry is.
